question: How can the whole also be partless?
premises: Then that one is called whole.
Its nature is complete grasping of object-subject interruption.
inference: The whole is partless through Śiva-yoga, whose nature is complete grasping that interrupts object and subject.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that one' is not specified in the verse.
The precise sense of the compound 'grāhyagrāhakavicchitti' is ambiguous.
plain_english: Then that [reality] is called whole, yet partless through Śiva-yoga, being of the nature of a complete grasping that interrupts object and subject.
